rounds.text: GK Energy Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated, trading at a modest P/E of 12.9x [E1] and 13.41x against its sector benchmark [E6], while offering exceptional capital efficiency through a 40.9% ROCE and a 36.8% ROE [E12, E13]. The business demonstrates robust top and bottom-line expansion, delivering a 75% compounded sales growth and a 171% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E14, E16]. This strong operating performance is further supported by an expanding operating margin that reached 20% by Mar 2026, marking a consistent four-year upward trend [E21, E23]. Market pricing completely disconnects from these fundamentals, as a reverse DCF indicates that today's price of ₹ 129 implies a mere 2.2% earnings growth against an 18.0% base-case assumption [E38], while a DCF intrinsic value sits significantly higher at ₹ 406 per share [E36]. Promoters remain firmly committed with a stable 79.20% holding [E32], and the company maintains a conservative financial profile with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.23x and reduced borrowings of ₹ 203 Cr [E29, E30]. Conceded: the stock currently sits below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside negative institutional money flow [E35, E41], and free cash flow stands at a negative ₹ -42 Cr due to weaker cash conversion [E25, E27].
